turns.prompt_text: Where in age can I go to get my Chevrolet Malibu raised up so that I can get under to do work myself and how much would that cost me?
turns.response_html:
It looks like "age" was a typo for Ames, where finding a dedicated self-service garage with a car lift is a bit tricky. While there aren't any commercial "DIY garages" currently operating directly in the Ames or Des Moines area, you have a few practical options for getting under your Malibu.

1. The Closest Dedicated DIY Facility

The nearest shop specifically designed for people to rent lifts and tools is DIY Garage.

  • Location: Omaha/Bellevue, NE (about a 2.5-hour drive from Ames).
  • Cost: Approximately $40 per hour for a bay with a lift and basic tools.
  • Best for: Major projects (like transmission work or exhaust replacement) where you absolutely need the height of a professional hydraulic lift and a "wingman" on-site for advice.

2. The Local "Buy Once" Alternative

Most DIYers in Ames tend to invest in their own lifting equipment. Since you have a Chevrolet Malibu (which has a relatively standard ground clearance), you can get the car high enough for oil changes, suspension work, or fuel line repairs using a home setup.

  • Where to go: Harbor Freight (on S Duff Ave in Ames) or AutoZone.
  • What to get: * High-Lift Ramps: Usually around $50–$70. Great for quick oil changes.
    • Floor Jack & Jack Stand Combo: A decent 3-ton set will cost you $100–$150.
  • Cost: A one-time investment of $150 is often cheaper than renting a bay and paying for gas to Omaha.

3. Professional Backup with a Discount

If you realize a project is more than you want to tackle on your back in a driveway, Campus Garage in Ames is highly rated for GM vehicles like the Malibu.

  • The Perk: They offer a 10% discount for ISU students and faculty.
  • Benefit: They have ASE-certified Master Technicians who specialize in Chevrolet, which is helpful if you run into a diagnostic issue you can't solve yourself.

4. Storage Unit Work-Around

Some car enthusiasts in town rent self-storage units (like those on East Lincoln Way) to store and work on project cars.

  • Warning: You must check the lease agreement first; many facilities forbid "active maintenance" (especially fluids) due to insurance and environmental regulations.
  • Cost: Usually $80–$150 per month for a unit large enough for a Malibu.

Pro-Tip for your Malibu: If you're working on the underside, remember that the Malibu has specific jacking points on the pinch welds. Using a "puck" or a grooved block on your jack stands will prevent you from bending the metal or damaging the rocker panels.

What kind of work are you planning to do on the Malibu?

turns.prompt_text: I'd like to install a hitch, a Curtis hitch
turns.response_html:
Installing a Curt Class 2 trailer hitch on your Chevrolet Malibu is a practical way to add towing or cargo capacity. Since you're planning to do the work yourself, you can expect to save significantly on labor while setting yourself up with a reliable connection for bike racks or light trailers.

Recommended Curt Hitches for your Malibu

For a 2016–2025 Chevrolet Malibu, the Curt 12185 is the standard fit. It is a Class 2 hitch with a 1-1/4" receiver, rated for 3,500 lbs of gross trailer weight and 350 lbs of tongue weight.

  • Curt Class 2 Trailer Hitch 12115: A robust light-duty option perfect for utility trailers or small boats.
  • Curt 12185 Hitch + Wiring Kit: This bundle includes the specific wiring harness needed for your Malibu, which is often required by law if you're towing a trailer.
  • CURT Class 2 Trailer Hitch + Ball Mount: A convenient kit that includes the ball mount, though you will still need to purchase the trailer ball separately.

Estimated Costs

Expense CategoryPrice RangeNotes
Hitch Parts$150 – $350Prices vary by vendor; bundles with wiring are more expensive.
DIY Tools$0 – $150Assuming you already have a basic socket set and torque wrench.
Professional Labor$75 – $150This is what you save by doing it yourself.

Installation Overview & Tools

Most Curt hitches for the Malibu are designed for a bolt-on installation, meaning you typically don't have to drill into the frame. However, you may need to temporarily lower the exhaust or trim a small section of the lower bumper fascia to get a perfect fit.

Essential Tools for the Job:

  • Socket Set & Ratchet: 13mm, 15mm, and 17/32" are common sizes for this vehicle.
  • Torque Wrench: Critical for tightening bolts to the exact specification (usually 37 lb-ft for smaller bolts and 110 lb-ft for larger ones).
  • Fishwire Tool: Usually included with the hitch to help thread bolts through the frame.
  • Aviation Shears: If your specific model requires trimming the plastic fascia.
  • Safety Glasses: Highly recommended when working directly under the vehicle.
